29.0.0.en: Moses reminded the people of the ten plagues with which God struck Pharaoh in order to deliver them from his bondage. Some of them had seen these plagues as children, and others had certainly heard of them from their fathers.

29.1.0.en: Moses grieves over the people's lack of faith in God's power and their lack of submission to Him, for they refused to enter the Promised Land and wandered in the wilderness forty years until those who refused had died.

29.1.1.en: God wants to reveal His wisdom to you and guide you in all your ways, if you love Him, give yourself to prayer and the reading of the Holy Bible, and remain steadfast in His Church. Do not neglect Him, lest He abandon you and you lose your sensitivity and understanding.

29.2.0.en: God worked a miracle for them in His care for them in the wilderness, for He preserved their clothes and their sandals for forty years. It is not natural for clothes or sandals to last so long, but it was the blessing of God (ch. 8:4).

29.3.0.en: Throughout the time of wandering in the wilderness they did not eat bread, which is the basic food necessary for bodily life, and they did not drink wine, which they think strengthens the body. Rather, their food was limited to the manna and their drink to the water that came out of the rock. Yet God preserved their health, so that they might know that He alone is the Giver of life and strength.

29.4.0.en: Moses returns to remind them of their victories over Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, and how they took possession of their lands, in which the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh settled. The credit for this was not theirs, but belonged to the Lord, who gave them this victory and helped them against their enemies.

29.5.0.en: Moses charges them to keep the words of the covenant and do them, and not to betray the covenant of the Lord which He made with them, so that they may prosper in their ways, that is, hold fast to God's commandments and His Law.

29.6.0.en: All the people stood to enter into the covenant with God, and it includes:

29.6.1.en: 1- Your leaders: the seventy elders, the judges, the heads of the tribes, the captains of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens, and the heads of the clans.

29.6.2.en: 2- Your tribes: the common people in all the tribes.

29.6.5.en: 5- The men of Israel: the adult males.

29.6.6.en: 6- The little ones: those under twenty years of age.

29.6.7.en: 7- Your wives: for the woman has a share in the blessings of the covenant just like the man.

29.6.8.en: 8- Your strangers: prisoners of war or slaves from any other peoples, or those who joined them from other peoples.

29.6.9.en: For God wants to make His covenant with all the groups of the people, because He is a Father to all.

29.6.10.en: And just as God called the children in the Old Testament to enjoy the privileges of the covenant even though they did not understand, so also the Church of the New Testament grants her children the privileges of the covenant of grace, represented by the Holy Sacraments, such as the sacrament of Baptism, the sacrament of Confirmation, the sacrament of Holy Communion, and so on.

29.7.0.en: Here God renews His covenant with His people, which He had previously made with their fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, so that they will be His people and be called by His name, and He will be a God to them who cares for them throughout their lives.

29.8.0.en: The covenant includes all the groups of the people with all their individuals, whether those present at the place or those absent for reasons of illness or old age, and not only the present generation but also the generations to come, that is, all believers, present and future.

29.8.1.en: God loves you and wants you to be a son to Him. You are not lost among the millions, but you have a place in the heart of God that no one else fills. So seize your opportunity, and pledge to live with Him and remain steadfast in His Church.

29.9.s.en: (3) The worship of idols and its punishment

29.9.0.en: Moses brings back to the people's memory what they themselves witnessed during their stay in the land of Egypt, and during their passing through the midst of the other Gentile peoples after leaving Egypt on their way to the Promised Land, as they crossed various regions inhabited by pagan peoples, and the detestable customs and practices they saw, and the idols made by hands of wood, stone and metals.

29.10.1.en: Absinthe: a plant whose juice is extremely bitter and also poisonous.

29.10.2.en: Root: a person or a deviant group from which misleading speech results.

29.10.3.en: The Lord warns them lest any individual or group among them fall into the worship of idols, so that he or the group turns away from attachment to the Lord to worship the gods of the Gentiles. Then he becomes a cause of stumbling for others who follow his example, and causes the fall of many souls, so that he is like the intense bitterness that spreads bitterness in the mouths of many if they taste it.

29.11.0.en: Bless himself in his heart: justify himself.

29.11.1.en: This person, or the deviant group that brings evil upon itself and upon the rest of the people, when the curse which the Lord swore to bring upon those who betray His covenant is read in his hearing, takes no heed of the evils he commits, but rather approves of his deeds, insisting on acting according to his own desires, heedless of the Lord's warnings, saying to himself, "I shall be safe, even if I insist on continuing in this conduct of mine." This stubborn person works to spread evil among the people, so that the wrath of the Lord falls on all, the careless and the simple, whom this deviant person led astray and enticed to walk in evil.

29.11.2.en: What is meant by "to add drunkenness to thirst" is that the green and the dry perish alike. The one who is watered is he who has committed many iniquities to the full, as one who is watered has drunk his fill of water. The thirsty is he who abstains from iniquities but was enticed by the deed of the wicked person until it destroyed him, and he perished with him.

29.12.0.en: The Lord will not spare this stubborn person who insists on worshiping idols, but will punish him with great wrath, like a fire that burns him so that smoke comes out of it, that is, God will destroy him and cast him into torment and the eternal fire. Thus the curses that are in the book of the covenant will fall upon him, and the Lord will destroy him and blot out his name from the earth.

29.13.0.en: Separate him unto evil: set him apart for evil.

29.13.1.en: The Lord sets him apart for all the plagues and woes that came in the curses mentioned in this book, so that misfortunes and afflictions fall upon him.

29.14.0.en: Your children in the generations to come, and the foreigners who come to your land from distant countries, will see what has befallen the land of Israel of plagues and diseases that the Lord allowed to come upon them, which are mentioned in the following verses.

29.15.0.en: Admah and Zeboiim: small towns surrounding Sodom and Gomorrah that were burned with them (Gen 14:

29.15.1.en: 1, 2, Gen 19.(Destruction will strike all its land and it will become unfit for cultivation. The good land, which used to flow with milk and honey, will be covered with sulfur, salt and the remains of burning, exactly as happened to Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim.

29.16.0.en: The other peoples, when they see the ruin that has befallen the land of Israel, ask in astonishment why the anger of the Lord was kindled against them to this great degree.

29.17.0.en: The answer to this question will be that the reason for it is their betrayal of their covenant with the Lord the God of their fathers, the covenant which they made with Him after He brought them out of the land of their bondage, Egypt.

29.18.0.en: And whom He had not given unto them: God did not permit them, but they are gods strange to them.

29.18.1.en: Their betrayal of the Lord consisted in their turning away from His worship and going to worship other gods strange to them and to their fathers, whom it was not for them to worship, for they are not their gods but the gods of pagan peoples and nations who do not know the true God as they have known and experienced Him.

29.19.0.en: The Lord was greatly angered against them and brought upon them the curses that He had stated to them in a covenant before they entered the land of Canaan, which are mentioned in this book.

29.20.0.en: Because of the intensity of the Lord's anger against them and His great displeasure at their conduct, He uprooted them from the Promised Land and emptied the holy land of them, because they had lost their worthiness of it by their turning away from Him, and He scattered them in other lands strange to them, so that they were dispersed and scattered throughout the world.

29.20.1.en: His words "as it is this day" mean the day on which the foreigners will see the ruin that has befallen the land.

29.21.0.en: The secret things: the hidden wisdom of God, which human beings cannot understand however much their discoveries increase. Those things which are revealed: God's laws and teachings and all that He discloses to our minds.

29.21.1.en: Moses charges his people to hold fast to the commandments of God and His laws that are revealed to them, and not to be troubled because of the existence of divine mysteries they do not understand, since they will not be able to grasp all the wisdom of God with their limited minds.

29.21.2.en: Obey God's commandments and do not worry about the future or any obscure matters you do not understand, but only ask for His help and care, for He is your Father who guides you in all that you need.

29.21.3.en: The blessings of repentance and keeping the commandments

30.0.0.en: If you experienced the blessings of God when you obeyed His commandments, but afterward fell into sins and the curses came upon you, you can return to God by repentance, and He will forgive you and give you the blessings mentioned in the following verses (vv. 3-10). Thus the mercies of God are shown, who gives hope to His children however much they sin.

30.0.1.en: It is beneficial for a person, if he falls and misfortunes come upon him, to remember the blessings he used to enjoy when he was obedient to God, so that he may regain them by repentance, as the prodigal son did (Lk 15:17).

30.1.0.en: The outmost parts of heaven: the farthest places on earth, where, when a person looks toward them, he sees the sky as if it meets the earth.

30.1.1.en: The first blessing for the repentant people, whom the enemies enslaved, took captive and scattered in the lands of the world, is that God gathers them in His mercies and brings them back to their homeland, as happened in the return from captivity at the hands of Zerubbabel, Ezra and Nehemiah, because if the wicked person's heart returns to God by repentance, He restores to him his freedom and dignity.

30.2.0.en: God brings the people back to the land of their fathers and multiplies them more than they were in the days of their glory, for God's blessings to the repentant surpass every blessing, and this is the second blessing.

30.3.0.en: The third blessing is a person's return to the covenant with God, not only by the circumcision of the flesh but by the circumcision of the heart, that is, devoting it to the love of God. Circumcision in the Old Testament signifies Baptism, which is the renewal of man's nature to live with God (Col 2:11, 12).

30.4.0.en: The Lord turns the curses upon your enemies who drove you out of the land and oppressed you. Though the Lord had used them as a rod of discipline for His people, when the people repent God removes from them the yoke of those who enslaved them, and even afflicts them as they afflicted His people, so that the people of God are exalted and the enemies weakened. This is the fourth blessing.

30.5.0.en: The Lord accepts their repentance when they return and obey His voice, walk according to His statutes and judgments, and live a life of obedience, and this is the fifth blessing.

30.6.0.en: The Lord's blessings increase and He floods them with good things, so that they prosper in every work to which their hands reach, and He blesses their offspring, the produce of their cattle and their sheep, the crops of their land and the fruit of their trees. And when the Lord turns from His anger, He rejoices in their good and prosperity as He had rejoiced in the prosperity of their fathers when they were subject to His obedience and doing His commandments, and this is the sixth blessing.

30.7.0.en: The book of the Law: the book of Deuteronomy, which Moses was delivering to them.

30.7.1.en: The good things and blessings are conditional upon returning to God, repentance, and obeying the commandments mentioned in the book of the Law.

30.7.2.en: It is to be noted that when he spoke in the previous chapter about the punishment of the wicked, he mentioned God by the name "Jehovah the Lord," that is, God the Existing and the Just, whereas in this chapter he mentions Him by the name "the Lord your God," that is, your own God who loves you and gives you many blessings when you repent and return to Him.

30.7.3.en: Do not be distressed by the consequences of your sins and your repeated falling, but rise quickly, confident that the blessings of repentance are greater than you imagine, because God loves you and wants your salvation.

30.8.0.en: The commandment is not hard or burdensome, but it is within their ability to apply it in their lives as long as they are ready to receive it, for grace works and supports a person and helps him to obey the commandment.

30.9.0.en: The duties required of the people of Israel toward God are not fearsome, in a place difficult to reach. They are not in heaven, so that one must search for someone to go up there and bring them to them, nor do they require crossing seas and oceans to obtain them and bring them to them, to be read in their hearing so that they may do them. And if God in the Old Testament gave His people a clear and understandable commandment to carry out, then in the New Testament the commandment became clearer still through the Incarnation of Christ, who fulfilled the commandment and lived as an example for us.

30.10.0.en: The Lord brought His word to man, for it is He who drew near to him with it and put it in his mouth, to repeat it to himself and to teach it to others, and to keep it in his heart to meditate on it and do it, so that it may be his guide in all his ways. St. Paul quoted these verses in (Rom 10:5-10) to affirm the importance of trusting in God, believing His word and acting on it.

30.10.1.en: Take care to read the Holy Bible and meditate on it every day, so that you may apply it in your life and live in peace.

30.11.0.en: Understand well what I say to you. Man is given a choice between two ways: the way of good, which leads him to life, and the way of evil, which leads to death. For man is free in will and may choose between the two ways.

30.11.1.en: Life here is the joyful earthly life and also the blessed eternal life, and death is physical death and also spiritual death and eternal perdition.

30.12.0.en: The Lord gave His people all the commandments that are able to lead them to a blessed earthly and eternal life. These commandments are summed up in that he should love the Lord with all his heart, walk in His ways, and keep His commandments, statutes and judgments. By this he lives and grows in grace and bears fruit and enjoys the Lord's blessings in the land which he is entering to possess. And this is the summary of the Ten Commandments as Christ Himself declared (Lk 10:27).

30.13.0.en: And on the contrary, if you turn away from Me in your hearts and do not listen to My voice, but go astray and go after other gods besides the Lord your God to worship them, then without doubt your destruction is certain and you will perish. Likewise I assure you that you will be deprived of the land which you are crossing the Jordan to possess, because the enemies will seize it and drive you out of it.

30.14.0.en: The Lord gives them His laws not in secret but openly before all, the heavenly and the earthly, and all living creatures bear witness that the Lord did not fall short in teaching them and warning them. And the Lord, in giving them a choice between the two ways in accordance with the principle of freedom given to man, nevertheless in His great love counsels them and urges them to choose life and blessing and to keep away from death and the curse.

30.15.0.en: The pillar of man's life is the love of the Lord, listening to His voice and attachment to Him, because God is the source of the life of all human beings, and He is our Creator, the origin of our existence and the Giver of all good things. And the Lord here promises them that their stay in the Promised Land will be long if they walk in His ways and obey His commandments.

30.15.1.en: You must choose the good yourself in order to obtain happiness on earth and in heaven, for happiness is within your reach if you seek it by cleaving to God and obeying His commandments.

30.15.2.en: The handing over of leadership to Joshua
